priorStories.headline: U.S. inflation reaches 3.7%
priorStories.body:
Consumer prices rose 0.6% in September and were 3.7% higher than a year earlier, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported.

Gasoline prices jumped 9.1% during the month and accounted for more than half of the overall increase. Prices excluding food and energy rose 0.3% for the month and 2.6% over the year.

priorStories.headline: Social Security benefits will rise 3.6%
priorStories.body:
About 76 million Social Security and Supplemental Security Income recipients will receive a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027.

Retirement benefits will increase by about $75 a month on average. The adjustment starts with January Social Security payments; higher SSI payments begin December 31.

priorStories.headline: Fighting puts aid beyond 800,000 Yemenis
priorStories.body:
Intensified fighting has put about 800,000 people beyond the World Food Programme’s reach. They include more than 600,000 aid-dependent residents of besieged Taiz.

The United Nations said more than 200,000 people had recently been displaced. The International Committee of the Red Cross reported unprecedented numbers of weapon-wounded patients at some front-line hospitals.

priorStories.headline: Two struck commercial ships sink near Hormuz
priorStories.body:
Maritime officials confirmed that two commercial ships struck by projectiles have sunk near the Strait of Hormuz.

The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride was struck while crossing the strait on October 13. All 21 crew members were evacuated without reported injuries. The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao sank weeks after a September 23 strike that killed one crew member.

Responsibility for the attacks had not been established.

priorStories.headline: Ireland’s public sector begins nationwide strike
priorStories.body:
About 300,000 teachers, health workers, civil servants and other public employees began Ireland’s first widespread public-sector strike since 2009 after pay talks stalled.

Emergency hospital departments and public transportation continued operating, but reduced health, fire and ambulance services caused widespread disruption. Thousands of medical procedures were canceled.

candidates.summary: A private school roof collapsed while classes were underway in Peshawar, killing at least 28 people, mostly children, according to initial reports from authorities and hospital officials. Dozens of people were injured, and reported casualty totals varied as rescue teams cleared the rubble.
candidates.title: School roof collapse kills children and teacher in Peshawar

candidates.summary: An overnight Russian attack killed three people and injured six in Ukraine’s Kirovohrad region, regional authorities said. Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched two missiles and 580 drones nationally from Wednesday evening into Thursday morning; it reported destroying or jamming 536 drones, with impacts recorded at 31 locations.
candidates.title: Russian drone attack kills three in central Ukraine

candidates.summary: Trudy strengthened into a Category 1 hurricane over the eastern Pacific, with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph. At 0900 UTC, the National Hurricane Center placed it about 300 miles south-southwest of Acapulco and forecast rapid intensification as it approached southwestern and west-central Mexico over the weekend.
candidates.title: Trudy strengthens into a hurricane south of Mexico

candidates.summary: Heavy rain that began Wednesday night flooded homes, roads and underpasses across Istanbul. The governor’s office reported three deaths and four people missing Thursday, while Turkey’s interior minister said more than 2,700 stranded people were evacuated. Schools remained closed, and officials said some districts received their heaviest rainfall since 1985.
candidates.title: Istanbul flooding kills three and prompts mass evacuations

candidates.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile over Medina province and separately destroyed a drone over Saudi Arabia’s Eastern province. The coalition did not assign responsibility for the missile, and Yemen’s Houthi movement denied carrying out the attack on Medina.
candidates.title: Saudi coalition reports intercepting missile over Medina

candidates.summary: Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in Russia’s Ryazan region, starting a fire, according to Russian officials. A senior Ukrainian official confirmed the strike to the Associated Press. Ukraine said it was resuming attacks on Russian oil facilities because Moscow had not observed a brief pause in attacks on energy targets.
candidates.title: Ukraine resumes refinery strikes with attack in Russia’s Ryazan region

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said the Pentagon would no longer livestream the scheduled firing-squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan. Immediate family members of victims may still attend the December 3 execution in person. The reversal followed criticism from Republican and Democratic officials and the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops.
candidates.title: Trump cancels planned livestream of Nidal Hasan execution

candidates.summary: A global sell-off in artificial-intelligence-related shares sent South Korea’s Kospi down 7.6% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 down 4.9%. U.S. markets were mixed by late Thursday morning: the Nasdaq was down 0.4%, while the Dow was up about 0.9%, as concerns centered on debt-funded AI investment and elevated bond yields.
candidates.title: AI stock sell-off drives steep declines in Asian markets

candidates.summary: An AP-NORC survey released ahead of the U.S. midterm elections found roughly eight in 10 registered voters disapproved of President Donald Trump’s handling of the cost of living and about three-quarters disapproved of his handling of the economy. About half wanted substantial change in how the country is governed, while roughly three in 10 wanted a complete overhaul.
candidates.title: AP-NORC poll finds broad dissatisfaction with Trump and economy
